question: A store holds 132 rollers and 124 pins, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test puck whose mass is 41 kg on a level air table. The energy the puck carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 6 identical pucks are launched per run the run energy is 6 times that value. The run energy is expressed in kilojoules and a calibration allowance of 22 kJ is then subtracted. The table is 1.5 m wide. What figure remains, in kJ?

The number the panel displays at the end is 12 kN less than 8 times the kilonewton reading described below. A hoist takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0 and reads it as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A cage of mass 144 kg is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must apply to the cage is calculated. A slack allowance of 21 N is subtracted from that force, and what is left, expressed in kilonewtons, is the reading in question. The shaft is 70 m deep. What number does the panel display, in kN?

A depot holds 380 rail clips and 150 keys, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test wagon whose mass is 42 kg on a level rail. The energy the wagon carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. A trigger circuit adds 23 kJ to that figure and a damper then absorbs 5 kJ. The depot repeats the run 10 times in a shift and the energies add. The rail is 25 m long. What is the shift total, in kJ?

The number the log ends with is 29 kJ more than a figure that is itself 25 kJ more than the kilojoule reading described below. A patch bay has 9 identical ports and any 2 of them may be linked; the number of different links available has 3 added to it, and the result is the release speed in metres per second of a test mass of 56000 g on the rail beside the bay. The energy that mass carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules to give that reading. The bay runs at 12 V. What number does the log end with, in kJ?

The value the panel shows at the end is 11 kN more than 8 times the kilonewton reading described below. A store holds 83 spindles and 181 collets, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to a carriage whose mass is 71000 g. The force the drive must apply to the carriage to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons to give that reading. What value does the panel show, in kN?

The figure the crane display ends on is the kilonewton form of the force described below. A hoist controller takes the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0 and reads it as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A cage of mass 95 kg is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must apply to the cage is calculated. Because 4 identical cages hang from one beam the beam force is 4 times that value, a tare of 3 N from the load cell is then added, and a further 11 N of shackle weight is added after that. What figure does the crane display end on, in kN?

The number the log ends with is 7 times the force described below. A conveyor controller takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0, subtracts 12 from it, adds 17 to the result, then adds 5 more, and reads what it gets as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A pallet of mass 197 kg is accelerated at that rate by the belt. The force the belt must apply to the pallet to accelerate it that hard is the force in question. What number does the log end with, in N?

Between the 2nd and the 3rd second of a stroke, a machine slide advances at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 1 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a test block whose mass is 60000 g. The energy the block carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. A damper absorbs 12 kJ of it, a trigger circuit then adds 30 kJ, and a brake finally removes 19 kJ. The slide is 0.8 m long. What energy remains, in kJ?

The number the bench totals at the end is 12 times the kilojoule reading described below. A workshop holds 17 dies and 273 blanks, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock; that batch size is multiplied by 12 to give the release speed in metres per second of a test puck whose mass is 13 kg. The puck runs on a level air table and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded. That energy, expressed in kilojoules, is the reading in question. What number does the bench total, in kJ?

The figure the rig prints last is the kilonewton form of the force described below. During the first second of a cycle, a linear drive advances at a rate equal to 1 times the square of the elapsed time plus 3 times the elapsed time. The total advance from the 0th to the 1st second, taken as a plain number, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a carriage whose mass is 142 kg. The force the drive must apply to the carriage is calculated and a tare of 11 N from the load cell is added to it. Because 11 identical carriages run from one frame, the frame load is 11 times that total, and that frame load is the force in question. What figure does the rig print last, in kN?

A control cabinet has 13 identical contactors and any 2 of them may close together; the number of different pairs available is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to a shuttle of mass 138000 g. The force the drive must apply to the shuttle to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and expressed in kilonewtons. A slack allowance of 1 kN is subtracted from it and a preload of 3 kN is then added. Because 9 identical shuttles run from one anchor wall, the wall load is 9 times what results. What is the load on the anchor wall, in kN?

A yard holds 259 chain links and 224 hooks, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to a wagon whose mass is 197000 g. The force the drive must apply to the wagon to accelerate it at that rate is calculated. Because 4 wagons run per drawbar, and 4 drawbars pull on one coupler, the coupler force is that value multiplied by 4 and then by 4 again. A slack allowance of 20 N is finally subtracted. What force does the coupler carry, in N?

A conveyor controller takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0 and doubles it to fix its acceleration in metres per second squared. A crate of mass 89000 g is accelerated at that rate by the belt, and the force the belt must apply to the crate is calculated. Because 8 identical crates ride the belt at once, the belt load is 8 times that force. The belt runs at 40 rpm. What is the belt load, in kN?

The number the rig totals at the end is 8 times a value that is itself 8 times the energy described below. A control desk has 6 identical keys and exactly 3 of them are pressed in any combination; the number of different combinations available is multiplied by 3 to give the release speed in metres per second of a puck whose mass is 27 kg on a level air table. The energy the puck carries because of its motion at that speed is the energy in question. What number does the rig total, in J?

A cam gives the follower displacement as 2 times the cube of the shaft angle plus 5 times the square of the shaft angle. The rate at which the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing, at a shaft angle of 2.0, is the release speed in metres per second of a slider whose mass is 13 kg. The energy the slider carries because of its motion is recorded. The machine launches 12 sliders per station, has 3 stations per line and 8 identical lines, and all the energies add. The shaft turns at 260 rpm. What is the total energy, in kJ?

A launcher takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0 and reads it as a release speed in metres per second. A dart of mass 58000 g is released at that speed along a level rail, and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded and expressed in kilojoules. A damper then absorbs 14 kJ of that figure, and a brake removes a further 13 kJ. The rail is 6 m long. What energy remains, in kJ?

A cam on a rolling mill gives the follower displacement as 4 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 3 times the square of the shaft angle. The rate at which the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing, at a shaft angle of 1.0, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 75 kg. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is calculated, 21 N of guide friction is subtracted from it, and a preload of 29 N is then added. Because 6 identical slides run from one frame, and 10 frames stand in the hall, the hall load is that figure multiplied by 6 and then by 10. The mill runs at 180 rpm. What is the hall load, in N?

The number the report ends on is 8 kJ less than the kilojoule figure described below. A control panel has 6 identical switches and exactly 4 of them are closed in any configuration; the number of different configurations available has 23 added to it, and the result is the release speed in metres per second of a test mass of 41 kg on the rail beside the panel. The energy that mass carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 4 identical masses are launched per run the run energy is 4 times that value. That run energy, expressed in kilojoules, is the figure in question. What number does the report end on, in kJ?

A workshop holds 257 spindles and 164 collets, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock. That batch size is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test trolley whose mass is 23000 g on a level bench. The energy the trolley carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 6 trolleys run per round and 7 rounds make a shift, all those energies add. The shift total is expressed in kilojoules and a calibration allowance of 6 kJ is then subtracted. What figure remains, in kJ?

The value the panel settles on is 30 kN more than the kilonewton reading described below. A hoist takes the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0 and reads it as an acceleration in metres per second squared. A cage of mass 126000 g is lifted with that acceleration and the force the cable must apply to the cage is calculated. A slack allowance of 22 N is subtracted from that force and a shackle weight of 15 N is then added, and what results, expressed in kilonewtons, is the reading in question. What value does the panel settle on, in kN?

The number the sheet ends with is 6 times a figure that is 13 J below the energy described here. A store holds 352 rollers and 327 pins, and both are issued in equal batches of the largest size that leaves nothing over in either stock; that batch size has 8 subtracted from it and 15 added to the result, giving the release speed in metres per second of a test puck whose mass is 12000 g. The energy the puck carries because of its motion on a level air table is the energy in question. The table is 1.3 m wide. What number does the sheet end with, in J?

A cam on a rolling mill gives the follower displacement as 4 times the cube of the shaft angle minus 2 times the square of the shaft angle. The rate at which the rate of change of that displacement is itself changing, at a shaft angle of 2.0, is the acceleration in metres per second squared given to a slide whose mass is 76 kg. The force the drive must apply to the slide to accelerate it at that rate is calculated and a preload of 30 N is added to it. The total is expressed in kilonewtons and multiplied by 8, because 8 identical slides run from one frame. A release mechanism then removes 11 kN from the frame load. What load remains, in kN?

The number the log ends with is 12 times a figure that is 27 kJ above the kilojoule reading described below. A launch controller adds its two dial settings 2 and 1 and multiplies the sum by 8 to fix the release speed, in metres per second, of a sled whose mass is 10000 g. The sled runs on a level rail and the energy it carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 4 identical sleds are launched per run the run energy is 4 times that value. That run energy, expressed in kilojoules, is the reading in question. The rail is 14 m long. What number does the log end with, in kJ?

A patch bay has 9 identical ports and any 2 of them may be linked; the number of different links available is the release speed, in metres per second, of a test mass of 41 kg on the rail beside it. The energy that mass carries because of its motion is recorded and a trigger coil then adds 22 J to it. The rig launches 9 identical masses in a run and the resulting energies add. That run total is expressed in kilojoules, and 9 identical runs make up the trial, with their energies adding. The bay is rated at 12 V. What is the trial total, in kJ?

Between the 1st and the 2nd second of a stroke, a machine slide advances at a rate equal to 2 times the square of the elapsed time plus 2 times the elapsed time. The total advance over that one-second interval, taken as a plain number, is the release speed in metres per second of a test block whose mass is 58000 g. The energy the block carries because of its motion is recorded, and because 5 identical blocks are launched per run the run energy is 5 times that value. The run energy is expressed in kilojoules and a calibration allowance of 25 kJ is then subtracted. The slide is 0.9 m long. What figure remains, in kJ?
